title: Qualitative Elemental Analysis: Lassaigne’s Sodium Fusion Tests
topics: Preparation of Lassaigne's Extract (Sodium Fusion Extract - SFE)
Detection of Nitrogen (NaCN + FeSO₄/FeCl₃ → Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃ Prussian Blue)
Detection of Sulfur (Na₂S + Sodium Nitroprusside → Na₄[Fe(CN)₅NOS] Purple/Violet)
Simultaneous Detection of Both N & S (NaSCN + Fe³⁺ → [Fe(SCN)]²⁺ Blood-Red Complex)
Detection of Halogens (AgCl white soluble, AgBr pale yellow, AgI yellow insoluble)
Detection of Phosphorus (Ammonium Phosphomolybdate Canary Yellow ppt)
quickSummary: Lassaigne's extract converts covalent N, S, X to NaCN, Na₂S, NaX. Nitrogen gives Prussian Blue Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃. Sulfur gives purple nitroprusside complex. Both N & S form blood-red [Fe(SCN)]²⁺ without Prussian blue. Phosphorus gives canary yellow phosphomolybdate.
summary: Master Lassaigne's sodium fusion extract preparation and qualitative detection of N, S, Halogens, and Phosphorus.

conceptBreakdown.title: 3.1 Sodium Fusion Extract (SFE) Formation

summaryBox.title: SFE Principles
summaryBox.takeaway: Converts covalent bonds to ionic sodium salts: Na + C + N → NaCN; 2Na + S → Na₂S; Na + X → NaX.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
LASSAIGNE'S EXTRACT QUALITATIVE TESTS
                                       │
     ┌──────────────────┬──────────────┴──────────────┬──────────────────┐
     ▼                  ▼                             ▼                  ▼
NITROGEN TEST          SULFUR TEST                   HALOGEN TEST        BOTH N & S PRESENT
NaCN + FeSO₄ →         Na₂S + Sodium Nitroprusside   Acidify with HNO₃,  Forms NaSCN →
Na₄[Fe(CN)₆]           → Purple/Violet Color         add AgNO₃:          yields Blood-Red Color
→ Prussian Blue        (Na₄[Fe(CN)₅NOS]).            ├── AgCl (White)    ([Fe(SCN)]²⁺) with
Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃.                                       ├── AgBr (Pale Yell)Fe³⁺ (No Prussian blue!).
                                                     └── AgI (Yellow)
conceptBreakdown.content:
To detect covalently bonded N, S, and halogens, the organic compound is fused with molten sodium metal:
$$\text{Na} + \text{C} + \text{N} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathbf{\text{NaCN}} \quad \vert \quad 2\text{Na} + \text{S} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathbf{\text{Na}_2\text{S}} \quad \vert \quad \text{Na} + \text{X} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathbf{\text{NaX}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Specific Chemical Detection Reactions
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Specific Chemical Detection Reactions
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
QUALITATIVE DETECTION REACTIONS

1. Nitrogen: 6 NaCN + FeSO₄ → Na₄[Fe(CN)₆] + Na₂SO₄
   Na₄[Fe(CN)₆] + 4 Fe³⁺ → Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃ ↓ (Prussian Blue)
2. Sulfur: Na₂S + Na₂[Fe(CN)₅NO] → Na₄[Fe(CN)₅NOS] (Purple/Violet)
3. Both N & S: Na + C + N + S → NaSCN
   Fe³⁺ + SCN⁻ → [Fe(SCN)]²⁺ (Blood-Red Complex, NO Prussian Blue!)
4. Halogens: SFE boiled with conc. HNO₃, then AgNO₃ added:
   • AgCl (White, soluble in NH₄OH)
   • AgBr (Pale yellow, sparingly soluble in NH₄OH)
   • AgI (Yellow, completely insoluble in NH₄OH)
5. Phosphorus: Fused with Na₂O₂ → Na₃PO₄ → conc. HNO₃ + Ammonium Molybdate → Canary Yellow (NH₄)₃PO₄ · 12 MoO₃
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Nitrogen Test**: $\text{NaCN}$ reacts with $\text{FeSO}_4$ and $\text{FeCl}_3$ in acid to produce insoluble **Prussian Blue / Ferriferrocyanide** ($\mathbf{\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]_3}$).
• **Sulfur Test**: $\text{Na}_2\text{S}$ reacts with Sodium Nitroprusside to yield a transient **Purple / Violet coloration** ($\mathbf{\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]}$).
• **Both N and S Present (CRITICAL TRAP)**: Sodium Thiocyanate ($\text{NaSCN}$) forms, which reacts with $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ to yield a **Blood-Red coloration** ($[\text{Fe(SCN)}]^{2+}$); **NO Prussian blue is produced!**
• **Halogen Tests**: SFE is first boiled with conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ to destroy $\text{CN}^-$ and $\text{S}^{2-}$ (preventing interference from $\text{AgCN}$/$\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$), then treated with $\text{AgNO}_3$.

quickRevision: Sulfur: Purple Na₄[Fe(CN)₅NOS] with sodium nitroprusside.
Both N & S: Blood-red [Fe(SCN)]²⁺ (no Prussian blue formed).
Boiling with HNO₃ decomposes NaCN and Na₂S prior to the halogen test.
Phosphorus gives a canary yellow ammonium phosphomolybdate precipitate.
